Emma: Quick RFC follow-up — proposal to terminate customer TLS at a regional 'opaque' proxy running in our managed VPCs to preserve customer source IP semantics for upstream services. High-level tradeoff: avoid maintaining per-customer peering/ENI sprawl vs. accepting TLS termination in our infra. Thoughts?
Diego: Curious — how exactly do we preserve source IPs after termination? If proxy talks to upstreams from our pool we usually SNAT.
Emma: Plan sketch: proxy terminates TLS, then uses an egress operator to bind flows to a per-tenant ephemeral 1:1 NAT mapping or route via a customer-affine ENI so upstreams see the original customer IP (or a stable mapped IP). Prefer eBPF-based tagging over iptables where possible.
Morgan: Security concern: terminating TLS inside our stack increases data exposure (PII/PCI). We need options for BYOK (customer-managed keys) or a passthrough/sni-only mode. Also audit logs and HSM-backed key usage mandatory for some customers.
Tara: From product POV we need three modes surfaced: `passthrough`, `sni-only`, `terminate` (with controls for BYOK and audit). Default should be `passthrough` to minimize risk.
Kevin: Config model sounds good. For rollout we should canary `terminate` with 2 pilot tenants, monitor auth logs and latency, then expand. Add a feature flag per-tenant.
Diego: Ops notes: if we go with NAT mapping approach we must ensure NAT table scale and cleanup. Example quick hack with iptables (not final):
```
# mark flows from proxy to upstream to avoid default SNAT
iptables -t mangle -A PREROUTING -m mark --mark 0x10 -j MARK --set-mark 0x10
iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -m mark --mark 0x10 -j ACCEPT
iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -s 10.0.0.0/22 -j MASQUERADE
```
Emma: Rather than iptables we prefer eBPF/XDP program that pins routes to ENIs and tags sockets, avoids heavy conntrack pressure. Diego will prototype eBPF to attach per-tenant policy.
SRE-bot: deploy-bot scheduled canary at 1755556700 — Emma/Diego please ack.
Diego: Ack. I'll deploy a canary in us-west-2 in a test account with two proxies and the egress operator.
Morgan: Also need a clear threat model doc + red-team checklist before turning on `terminate` for prod tenants. I'll own gating.
Tara: Naming bikeshed: calling it "Opaque Endpoint" in docs? Keep consumer-facing name neutral.
Emma: Action items: I will update the RFC with a new section for "Opaque Endpoint" behavior, rollout checklist, and BYOK integration notes. Diego: eBPF PoC + cleanup TTL policy (suggest 5m idle). Morgan: security checklist + audit requirements. Tara: product matrix and enabled-by-default flag.
Kevin: Metrics to track: p99 latency delta, p95/p99 error rate, egress IP count per-region, ENI allocation, conntrack table usage. Add alerts for NAT table pressure and ENI exhaustion.
Diego: Runtime edge-case: if customers rotate client certs frequently we could leak ephemeral NAT mappings. Plan to expire mappings after N seconds of idle (proposal 300s) and evict on rotation events.
Emma: Good call — set TTL 300s for now, revisit after canary.
SRE-bot: canary started 1755556725 — 2 proxies up in us-west-2 (test).
Diego: Observability from canary: p90 +8ms, p99 +22ms. No retries from upstream. ENI usage within limits.
Morgan: Security pre-audit passed for test tenants. OK to expand to 10-customer canary.
Tara: Docs note — we must clearly state which mode affects customer SLA and what logs/audit we provide.
Emma: Thanks all. I'll open the RFC follow-up PR and tag infra/security for approvals, and post the link in this thread when ready.
Kevin: One more: consider fallback path if egress operator fails (fall back to SNAT with clear telemetry). Add automatic rollback if auth errors spike.
Emma: Will add rollback policy and detection thresholds to the checklist.
Tara: :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: canary complete 1755556778 — no regressions; expanding to staged rollout per checklist.
Diego: Spinning next batch.
Morgan: I'll schedule red-team review for next week.
Emma: Closing notes: RFC diff will include diagrams (proxy placement, egress-operator control plane, keyflow) + migration playbook. Will ping reviewers.
